data.title: Theravance Shareholders Approve Merger with Zymeworks Inc.
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Theravance Biopharma ( (TBPH) ).

Theravance Biopharma held an extraordinary general meeting on September 18, 2026, at which shareholders voted on proposals tied to a planned merger with Zymeworks Inc., under a June 28, 2026 Merger Agreement that will make Theravance a wholly owned subsidiary of Zymeworks. With 79.14% of outstanding ordinary shares represented, investors approved the core merger proposal, including amendments to Theravance’s governing documents and capital structure, as well as a non-binding advisory vote supporting merger-related executive compensation, clearing a key closing condition for the transaction, which is expected to be completed on or about September 23, 2026, subject to remaining conditions.

The approval of the merger proposals positions Theravance to integrate into Zymeworks’ corporate structure, potentially reshaping its operational autonomy and strategic direction while giving shareholders a path to realize value via the agreed terms. The strong shareholder turnout and decisive support for both the transaction and related compensation packages signal broad investor backing for the deal, though completion remains contingent on satisfaction or waiver of all remaining closing conditions in the merger agreement.

data.title: Poste Italiane Takes Control of Telecom Italia, Becomes Indirect Owner of TIM Brasil
data.description:
The latest update is out from TIM S.A. ( (BR:TIMS3) ).

TIM S.A. announced that Italian postal and financial group Poste Italiane has acquired control of Telecom Italia through a voluntary public offer, reaching approximately 66.6% of the company’s share capital. As Telecom Italia’s new controlling shareholder, Poste Italiane now indirectly controls TIM Brasil, signaling a significant shift in the ownership structure that may influence the Brazilian operator’s strategic direction and governance.

The company noted that the acceptance period for the offer will reopen from September 21 to 25, allowing additional Telecom Italia shareholders to participate under the same terms. TIM S.A. stated it will continue to inform shareholders and the market of any relevant developments, underscoring the importance of this transaction for stakeholders monitoring changes in the broader Telecom Italia corporate group.

data.title: Santacruz Silver Buys 500-tpd Bolivian Mill to Boost Processing Capacity
data.description:
Santacruz Silver Mining ( (TSE:SCZ) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 18, 2026, Santacruz Silver Mining Ltd. said it had completed the acquisition of a 500-tonne-per-day milling facility in Bolivia, made up of two 250-tonne-per-day circuits with selective flotation systems for lead and zinc with high-grade silver. The plant will be dedicated to ore from its wholly owned Bolivian subsidiary San Lucas, expanding processing capacity to support the company’s growing third-party ore-sourcing business.

By shifting San Lucas material to the new plant, Santacruz plans to free capacity at its three existing mine processing facilities in Bolivia, enabling higher output from its own mines and advancing development plans. The facility, located about 5 kilometres from the Reserva mine, is expected to be commissioned in the fourth quarter of 2026 and reach commercial production by year-end, with a total investment of about US$14 million, including a US$9.2 million purchase price and US$4.8 million for upgrades and working capital.

data.title: Frontier Lithium Restructures Convertible Loan to Extend Maturity and Cut Conversion Price
data.description:
Frontier Lithium ( (TSE:FL) ) just unveiled an update.

Frontier Lithium Inc. has restructured its unsecured convertible loan by issuing a replacement agreement that capitalizes $279,720 of accrued interest into a new principal of $3,629,720, extends the maturity date by 18 months to February 25, 2028, and lowers the conversion price from $0.65 to $0.455 per share, without raising additional funds. The move, approved after the lender affiliated with board chairman Reginald Walker abstained from deliberations, is intended to enhance financial flexibility as the company advances its PAK Lithium Project, while relying on related-party transaction exemptions given the deal’s size relative to its market capitalization.

The restructuring underscores Frontier Lithium’s effort to shore up its capital structure during a capital-intensive pre-production phase, potentially making the debt more attractive to convert while deferring near-term repayment pressure. By securing more accommodative terms from an insider-affiliated lender and avoiding finder fees, the company aims to align stakeholder interests and maintain momentum on project development, though the reduced conversion price may introduce incremental dilution risk for existing shareholders if the loan is converted.
